note:
ISO 2026-W07 runs from February 9 through February 15. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 0.9° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌗 Last Quarter — 12:43:07 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Alhena, Sirius, α Pic as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -10.3; direct motion; 55.2% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Pluto in ecliptic longitude Feb 15 14:09 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude -1.2; direct motion; 86.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: In solar glare; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 99.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: In solar glare; magnitude 1.1; direct motion; 99.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.1; direct motion; 97.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.6; retrograde motion; 99.7% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 1.0; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.7; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: In solar glare; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Feb 15 14:09 UTC.

**Binoculars:** Trace Monoceros’s charted figure in the finder, then identify β Mon at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** Concentrate on M41. Increase magnification only after the target and surrounding pattern are secure.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

story_candidates.dek: β Mon is a stellar reference in Mon used by the weekly observing calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected β Mon for this week’s fixed-sky observing sequence; its permanent object identity ties the weekly entry to the same star used by the finder.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Mon constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.
